title: Give a Meal its vector, without giving anything a write path it should not have
objective: The embedding capability in the provider registry, and the one Edge Function in Kafoo that holds a service-role key on an AI path.
acceptance_criteria: the registry gains an embedding capability; Anthropic and OpenAI adapters either implement it or declare they cannot, and registry_test.ts covers a half-added provider and a wrong-provider fallback
embed-meal takes a Meal id and NOTHING else, and reads title and description FROM THE DATABASE — a client-supplied text field is ignored, proven by test
embed-meal writes meals.embedding and no other column
publishing a Meal succeeds when the provider is unreachable, leaving the Meal without a vector
ai-boundary-reviewer AND rls-reviewer have reviewed the diff and signed off before merge (T214)
notes:
The only thing in Kafoo on an AI path holding a service-role key. The argument for it is in plan.md's Complexity Tracking: an embedding is not a claim, so Principle II is not what stops it. That argument must be checked by something other than the document making it, which is why T214 is an acceptance criterion rather than a nicety. The manipulation hole it closes is real and invisible: a client that supplies the vector can supply the one nearest every query, and that Cook's Meal ranks first for everything, permanently.
